spec.name: attn_qwen2_5_0p5b
spec.description: Single attention head for one decode step: q.k scores over up to 256 cached positions, softmax, and the weighted sum of V over head_dim 64

derivation.rule: head_dim from the model; capacity and the score and weight formats from the softmax block; the output requantizer and accumulator widths from the MAC and requantizer blocks

ports.name: start
ports.desc: run the head over n cached positions

ports.name: shift_s
ports.desc: score shift: q.k to the softmax score format

ports.name: o_valid
ports.desc: an output element is on o_data

ports.name: o_index
ports.desc: which element of the head's output

behavior: Each cycle with load_valid high writes load_data into the query buffer at the next index, starting from 0 after reset and after every run, so q[0..63] are loaded in order before start.

start is a one-cycle pulse, with n, shift_s, scale_o and shift_o held stable for the whole run. busy must be high on the clock edge that samples start, so it already reads 1 one cycle later, and it stays high until the last output has been emitted.

The key and value caches are row-major: element d of position j is at address j*64 + d in both. k_data and v_data are registered reads: each carries the element at address a on the cycle after k_addr or v_addr = a. If the address is itself a register, that is two clock edges after the edge that loads a into it.

Scores: for j in 0..n-1, t_j = sum over d of q[d] * K[j][d], a signed 29-bit dot product. s_j = (t_j + 2**(shift_s-1)) >>> shift_s when shift_s > 0, else t_j, then clamped to [-2048, 2047]. The clamp is half the 13-bit score range so that a score minus the row maximum always fits the exponential's input.
Weights: w = softmax(s) over the n scores, exactly as the supplied softmax block computes it: 16-bit unsigned Q0.15, where 32768 is 1.0.

Output: for d in 0..63, a_d = sum over j of w_j * V[j][d], with w_j unsigned and V signed, then o_d = requant(a_d, scale_o, shift_o): multiply by scale_o, add 2**(shift_o-1) when shift_o > 0, arithmetic shift right by shift_o, saturate to [-128, 127]. The weights sum to under 2.0, so |a_d| stays under 2**23: a 24-bit signed sum, sign-extended into the requantizer's 29-bit input.
Emit each o_d with o_index = d and o_valid high for exactly that one cycle. Outputs may come in any order, but each index exactly once, and o_valid must be low at every other time.

The scores and weights are held in memories named sbuf and pbuf, declared reg signed [12:0] sbuf [0:255] and reg [15:0] pbuf [0:255], with position j at index j. The testbench reads them directly to check the scores and the softmax, so these names and layouts are part of the interface.

matvec, mac, softmax and requant are separate modules supplied as source files, not something to write. Instantiate them with exactly these ports, connected by name: matvec (input clk, input rst_n, input start, input [12:0] depth, input [12:0] cols, output [12:0] a_addr, output [25:0] w_addr, output mac_valid, output mac_clear, output col_valid, output [12:0] col_index, output busy); mac (input clk, input rst_n, input clear, input signed [7:0] a, input signed [7:0] b, input valid_in, output signed [28:0] acc, output valid_out); softmax (input clk, input rst_n, input start, input [8:0] n, output [7:0] s_addr, input signed [12:0] s_data, output w_valid, output [7:0] w_index, output [15:0] w_data, output busy); requant (input clk, input rst_n, input signed [28:0] acc_in, input [17:0] scale, input [6:0] shift, input valid_in, output signed [7:0] q_out, output sat, output valid_out).

matvec walks a_addr 0..depth-1 and w_addr col*depth onward for each of cols columns, drives mac_valid one cycle behind the address, pulses mac_clear between columns, and pulses col_valid with col_index when a column's sum is on the MAC's acc. Wire mac_valid to the MAC's valid_in and mac_clear to its clear. With depth = 64 and cols = n, matvec's w_addr is exactly the key address. softmax reads scores through s_addr and a registered s_data and emits w_valid, w_index and w_data. requant has a latency of exactly 9 cycles.
The weighted sum multiplies a 16-bit unsigned weight by an 8-bit signed value, which the 8-bit MAC cannot do, so it is its own multiply-accumulate.
All state resets to zero: busy and o_valid are 0 during reset.
